# professional-game-art-direction

Type: art-direction
Version: v0.2
Updated: 2026-07-08 13:37:48 +08:00
Status: draft for owner review

## Purpose

This file defines the professional art direction for the first playable
AI-PET-WORLD map. It answers what "professional game map" means before the
model draws and before review accepts a frame.

## First-Version Art Direction

| Field | Requirement |
|---|---|
| genre read | Cozy natural home / playable world map, not poster art. |
| camera | Top-down or slight three-quarter 2D game camera. |
| style | Hand-painted readable game map, not raw noise, collage, or photo mix. |
| mood | Alive, natural, gentle, exploratory, clean enough for gameplay. |
| primary read | Entrance to path to home center, then water edge and boundary. |
| material language | Earth-like grass, soil, water, stone and vegetation. |
| object language | Grounded objects with shared scale, light, palette and contact. |
| detail density | Detailed enough to feel rich, controlled enough to preserve playability. |

## Professional Standards

| Standard | Pass condition |
|---|---|
| first-glance game read | Viewer immediately reads it as a game map. |
| style unity | Terrain, objects and water share one art direction. |
| spatial clarity | Route, center, water and boundary are readable. |
| material clarity | Grass, path, water, shore and objects each read correctly. |
| object grounding | Trees, rocks and shrubs belong to the ground. |
| gameplay fit | Player can imagine movement and interaction. |
| polish | No placeholder feeling, no debug texture, no accidental artifacts. |

## Forbidden Looks

| Forbidden look | Reason |
|---|---|
| noise map | Texture exists but game structure is absent. |
| asset collage | Pieces look pasted from different sources. |
| sticker objects | Objects lack footprint, contact shadow or palette integration. |
| photo-like patchwork | Materials do not share game-art abstraction. |
| training preview | Image looks like an experiment instead of a player-facing frame. |
| decorative wallpaper | Pretty texture without playable route or center. |

## Hard failures:

| Failure | Meaning |
|---|---|
| art_direction_missing | Frame has no stable professional game art direction. |
| not_player_facing_art | Frame looks like training output or debug preview, not a player-facing map. |
| style_family_mixed | Terrain, objects or water belong to conflicting art styles. |
| gameplay_read_not_supported | Art direction does not support route, movement or interaction readability. |
| detail_density_unprofessional | Detail density is either empty, noisy, or uncontrolled. |

entries.content:
# earth

Type: world baseline
Version: v0.1

The first AI-PET-WORLD natural home uses Earth-like natural logic. This does
not mean photo realism. It means players should recognize water, soil, plants,
stone, light, and gravity through familiar Earth rules.

| Field | Definition |
|---|---|
| gravity | Earth-like. Trees, rocks, flowers, shrubs and small props must sit on ground. No floating objects. |
| light | Daylight natural outdoor light. Shadows must imply one shared world. |
| atmosphere | Clear, mild, natural-home climate. No alien fog, neon haze, fire sky, snow, desert, volcano or sci-fi atmosphere in v1. |
| water_behavior | Water is continuous, lower than land, visually wet at its edge, and not broken into random blue noise. |
| soil_behavior | Soil can be grass base, dirt path, damp shoreline, mud patch or exposed earth. Soil transitions should be irregular and natural. |
| plant_behavior | Plants grow from soil. Grass, shrubs, flowers and trees need root/ground contact cues. |
| stone_behavior | Rocks have weight, volume, contact shadow, and stable placement. |
| erosion | Path edges, shoreline edges and muddy transitions should be broken and organic, not straight hard cuts. |
| scale | Terrain and objects must share a consistent game scale. |
| camera | One consistent top-down or slight three-quarter map camera. No mixed perspective. |

Hard failures:

| Failure | Meaning |
|---|---|
| floating_object | Object appears pasted without ground contact. |
| mixed_world_physics | Some elements behave like icons, others like 3D objects, breaking world consistency. |
| non_earth_visual_logic | Water, soil, plant or stone no longer reads as Earth-like natural material. |

# game-map-composition-recipe

Type: composition-recipe
Version: v0.2
Updated: 2026-07-08 13:37:48 +08:00
Status: draft for owner review

## Purpose

This file defines how to compose the complete first playable map. Composition is
the bridge between world structure and what the player reads first.

## Composition Recipe

| Stage | Requirement |
|---|---|
| big shapes | Establish land mass, water region, boundary and open playable area. |
| route read | Place entrance, main path, home center and branch path before detail. |
| focal hierarchy | Home center and route must beat decorative clusters. |
| balance | Water, forest edge and object clusters frame the map without swallowing it. |
| negative space | Leave enough open playable grass/clearing for movement. |
| detail rhythm | Detail clusters should guide the eye, not scatter randomly. |
| final read | Player reads map route before micro texture. |

## Read Order

| Order | Player should read |
|---|---|
| 1 | This is a playable natural-home map. |
| 2 | Here is the entrance/start. |
| 3 | Here is the main route. |
| 4 | Here is the home center/main focus. |
| 5 | Here is water/shore and boundary. |
| 6 | Here are supporting objects and future interaction hints. |

## Composition Data Fields

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| focalPoint | Main readable target. |
| readOrder | Ordered list of visual priorities. |
| routeShape | Path graph and curve/width behavior. |
| massBalance | Land/water/boundary proportion. |
| negativeSpacePlan | Open areas reserved for gameplay readability. |
| detailClusterPlan | Where detail is allowed and where it must be sparse. |
| edgeFramePlan | How natural boundary frames the map. |

## Hard failures:

| Failure | Meaning |
|---|---|
| composition_recipe_missing | Generation task has no composition recipe. |
| read_order_failed | Player cannot read entrance, route, center, water and boundary in order. |
| focal_hierarchy_failed | Decorative details beat the main route or center. |
| negative_space_missing | Map has no readable open playable space. |
| detail_rhythm_random | Detail distribution feels random rather than composed. |

# layer-order

Type: composition rule
Version: v0.1

The first world map must be composed in readable game layers. A professional
game map is not a single noisy texture with objects pasted on top. Each visual
element must belong to a stable layer so runtime, collision and player reading
can agree.

## Required Layer Order

| Order | Layer | Requirement |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | base terrain | Grass, dirt, water and mud define the broad world surface. |
| 2 | terrain transition | Shoreline, path edge, mud edge and forest edge soften borders. |
| 3 | ground detail | Grass-detail, pebble, flower and reed add scale without blocking. |
| 4 | object base | Contact shadow, darker grass base or root base anchors objects. |
| 5 | solid object | Tree, shrub, rock and other collision objects sit above terrain. |
| 6 | readable highlight | Small light/color accents guide attention without becoming UI. |

## Professional Standard

| Standard | Meaning |
|---|---|
| readable_at_first_glance | A viewer can identify grass, path, water, trees and rocks in one second. |
| no_texture_soup | The map cannot look like one merged noise layer. |
| no_sticker_stack | Objects cannot look like unrelated images placed on a background. |
| no_collision_confusion | Solid objects and walkable areas must be visually different. |

Hard failures:

| Failure | Meaning |
|---|---|
| collapsed_layers | Terrain, details and objects visually merge into unreadable noise. |
| pasted_objects | Objects appear as stickers without contact or shared light. |
| layer_order_conflict | Details cover important path/water/object edges in a way that breaks reading. |

entries.content:
# map-readability

Type: composition rule
Version: v0.1

The map must read as a playable world before it reads as a painting. This means
the viewer can understand where the player starts, where the center is, where
paths lead, where water begins, and which places are blocked.

## Required Reading Order

| Step | Player Should Understand |
|---:|---|
| 1 | This is an outdoor Earth-like natural area. |
| 2 | There is a clear entrance into the map. |
| 3 | A main path leads to a home-center or central clearing. |
| 4 | A branch path or edge leads toward water or another point of interest. |
| 5 | Trees, rocks and water create natural boundaries. |
| 6 | Grass/path areas are playable while dense boundary objects are not. |

## Visual Contrast Targets

| Contrast | Requirement |
|---|---|
| path_vs_grass | Path must be warmer/browner and smoother than surrounding grass. |
| water_vs_land | Water must be cooler/bluer and visibly separated by shoreline. |
| object_vs_ground | Trees/rocks/shrubs must have clear silhouettes and grounding. |
| detail_vs_noise | Small details must support texture, not hide structure. |

Hard failures:

| Failure | Meaning |
|---|---|
| no_clear_route | Path route cannot be followed. |
| no_clear_center | Home-center/central clearing cannot be identified. |
| water_land_confusion | Water and land are visually confused. |
| professional_read_fail | The image may be decorative but does not read as a playable map. |

# professional-quality

Type: composition rule
Version: v0.1

This file defines the first human-level visual bar. It is stricter than the
current machine gate. A generated frame can pass machine checks and still fail
professional quality.

## Minimum Professional Bar

| Area | Pass Standard |
|---|---|
| style unity | Terrain and objects share one camera, lighting and rendering language. |
| material clarity | Grass, water, dirt, stone and plant material are immediately recognizable. |
| game readability | The map has navigable structure, not only a textured surface. |
| object grounding | Every object has base contact, contact shadow or embedded edge. |
| composition | Entrance, path, center, water and boundary form a coherent map. |
| polish | No placeholder blocks, broken decodes, harsh seams or obvious random noise. |

## First-Version Fail Examples

| Failure | Reason |
|---|---|
| image looks like terrain noise | It has material color but no game map structure. |
| image looks like collage | It lacks one shared camera/light/material language. |
| road floats above grass | Path is not integrated into terrain. |
| objects are inconsistent scale | Map cannot support gameplay collision or player navigation. |
| water edge is a vertical wall | It breaks top-down/slight three-quarter map logic unless explicitly designed. |

Hard failures:

| Failure | Meaning |
|---|---|
| not_game_ready | Does not look ready for a first playable game map. |
| no_art_direction | No stable visual language is visible. |
| target_not_learned | Repeated outputs ignore this dictionary and require training/data adjustment. |

# storage-plan

Type: database plan
Version: v0.1
Updated: 2026-07-08 12:52:59 +08:00

The visual data dictionary starts as versioned project documents, but it must be
designed for future database storage. The database will become the runtime
source of truth after the schema, migration path and sync rules are approved.

## Storage Phases

| Phase | Source of Truth | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| phase_1_document_first | Markdown files in this directory | Human-readable review, fast iteration, owner approval. |
| phase_2_structured_export | JSON generated from this dictionary | Program reads stable structured rules without manual parsing. |
| phase_3_database_mirror | Database tables mirror approved dictionary versions | Runtime and tools query rules by id/version. |
| phase_4_database_primary | Database becomes primary, documents are generated/exported views | Small model, runtime review and admin tools share one rule store. |

Phase 1 is the current project state. Do not jump directly to phase 4 before
schema, migration, rollback and review workflows are defined.

## Planned Tables

| Table | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `visual_dictionary_versions` | One approved dictionary release, such as `mvp-natural-home-v0.1`. |
| `visual_dictionary_entries` | Terrain, object, structure, style, composition and training entries. |
| `visual_dictionary_fields` | Structured fields for each entry, such as placement, scale and material rules. |
| `world_ontology_entities` | Entity taxonomy, allowed scopes, and source fact binding rules. |
| `spatial_grid_contracts` | Coordinate, layer, walkable, collision, and interaction contracts. |
| `map_grammar_parts` | Required complete-map parts such as entrance, route, center and boundary. |
| `ecology_state_rules` | Moisture, growth, vegetation density, water influence and biome continuity rules. |
| `gameplay_contracts` | Player readability, movement, collision, interaction and scale contracts. |
| `runtime_state_bindings` | worldId, tick, state diff, RuntimeFrame and review linkage. |
| `director_contracts` | Scene intent, plan outputs, generation conditions and fix-plan rules. |
| `generation_task_packages` | Structured local-model inference input packages and storage contracts. |
| `visual_failure_codes` | Stable failure codes used by machine review and owner review. |
| `visual_training_labels` | Positive/negative/pending labels used by training datasets. |
| `visual_review_records` | Every inference, generated image, owner review and machine review event. |
| `visual_review_record_labels` | Many-to-many labels attached to review records. |
| `visual_review_record_failures` | Many-to-many failure codes attached to review records. |
| `visual_model_checkpoints` | Local model/checkpoint identity, metrics and training lineage. |
| `visual_generated_assets` | Stored images, manifests, previews and runtime-frame references. |

## Core Entity Boundaries

| Entity | Must Not Contain |
|---|---|
| dictionary version | Raw images or model weights. |
| dictionary entry | Per-run inference results. |
| world ontology entity | Rendered pixels without source fact binding. |
| spatial grid contract | Decorative style rules that belong in visual-style. |
| map grammar part | Per-model checkpoint metrics. |
| generation task package | Owner final approval status without review record. |
| failure code | Long owner conversation history. |
| review record | Full binary image blob when file/object storage path is enough. |
| generated asset | Rule definitions that belong in dictionary entries. |
| model checkpoint | Owner review decisions that belong in review records. |

## Required IDs

| ID | Format |
|---|---|
| dictionaryVersionId | Stable kebab-case, for example `mvp-natural-home-v0.1`. |
| dictionaryEntryId | Stable path-like id, for example `terrain/grass`. |
| failureCode | Stable snake_case, for example `not_game_ready`. |
| trainingLabel | Stable snake_case, for example `negative_machine_pass_owner_fail`. |
| reviewRecordId | Timestamp plus run id or UUID. |
| modelCheckpointId | Model family plus version/checkpoint. |
| assetId | Stable id linked to image path and content hash. |

## Versioning Rules

| Rule | Requirement |
|---|---|
| immutable_approved_version | Approved dictionary versions cannot be silently edited. |
| draft_can_change | Draft versions can change until owner/project approval. |
| migration_required | Any schema change requires a migration note. |
| runtime_records_keep_version | Every review record stores the dictionary version used at review time. |
| model_training_keeps_version | Every dataset/model checkpoint stores the dictionary version used to create labels. |

## Sync Rules

| Direction | Rule |
|---|---|

## Purpose

This file defines the visual director layer. The director is not the local image
model and not the final reviewer. It translates world facts, dictionary rules,
and previous failures into a structured generation task.

## Director Inputs

| Input | Meaning |
|---|---|
| worldRuntimeSaveRecord | Current world facts, tick, owner, and world id. |
| visualFactManifest | Readable fact list for image planning. |
| dictionaryVersion | Current visual dictionary rules. |
| targetPolicy | First playable map target and hard restrictions. |
| latestFixPlan | Most recent failed review repair targets. |
| modelStatus | Whether the local model can generate and which checkpoint it uses. |

## Director Outputs

| Output | Meaning |
|---|---|
| sceneIntent | What this frame must express. |
| compositionPlan | How entrance, route, center, water, and boundary should read. |
| terrainPlan | How terrain layers should be expressed. |
| assetPlan | Which objects/resources may appear. |
| motionPlan | Reserved live-world movement or state expression. |
| generationCondition | Machine-readable input for local inference. |
| visualFixHints | Repair targets from failed reviews. |

## Professional Director Rules

| Rule | Requirement |
|---|---|
| structure before decoration | Entrance, route, center, water edge, and boundary are more important than details. |
| fact before beauty | The director may improve expression but cannot invent world facts. |
| failure reuse | Every failed review must become a specific next generation constraint. |
| no bypass | Director cannot mark a frame player-visible. Only review and RuntimeFrame gates can. |
| owner standard | Owner rejection is a valid training signal and must not be overwritten by machine pass. |

## Director Review Questions

| Question | Must be answerable |
|---|---|
| What is the main scene intent? | Yes. |
| Which world facts are visible? | Yes. |
| Which map grammar parts are required? | Yes. |
| Which previous failures are being repaired? | Yes. |
| Which parts are forbidden in this version? | Yes. |
| Can this be shown to player directly? | Always no at director stage. |

| Failure | Meaning |
|---|---|
| director_invents_world_fact | Director adds a fact not present in runtime state or version scope. |

# ai-drawing-process

Type: drawing-method
Version: v0.2
Updated: 2026-07-08 13:37:48 +08:00
Status: draft for owner review

## Purpose

This file defines how an AI system should think when drawing a complete game
map. These steps must become data for the local model, director, review system,
and training records. The model must not receive only a loose prompt. It must
receive drawing-process data.

## Drawing Process

| Step | Data needed | Output |
|---|---|---|
| 1. intent lock | game type, player view, frame purpose, dictionary version | clear image goal |
| 2. semantic inventory | terrain, objects, structures, resources, state facts | allowed visible entities |
| 3. spatial blocking | entrance, route, center, water edge, boundary, open areas | map layout blockout |
| 4. camera and scale | top-down/slight 3/4, object scale, path width, player scale | consistent viewpoint |
| 5. value grouping | light/dark grouping, route contrast, center clarity | readable first glance |
| 6. color script | grass/water/path palette, palette harmony, forbidden colors | unified color language |
| 7. material pass | grass texture, water detail, dirt path, shoreline, objects | readable materials |
| 8. grounding pass | object footprints, contact shadows, edge integration | no sticker/floating objects |
| 9. polish pass | detail density, edge accents, focal clarity, noise removal | professional game polish |
| 10. review pass | failure codes, score, next fix targets, storage | training feedback record |

## Required Drawing Data

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| imageGoal | What the frame must achieve for the player. |
| semanticInventory | What is allowed and required in the image. |
| spatialBlockout | Large-shape layout before details. |
| cameraScale | Camera angle, object scale and player-scale assumptions. |
| valuePlan | Readability plan using contrast and brightness. |
| colorPlan | Palette plan for all major materials. |
| materialPlan | How each material should be painted. |
| groundingPlan | How objects connect to terrain. |
| polishPlan | How final detail is controlled. |
| reviewPlan | How pass/fail is judged and stored. |

## AI Drawing Rule

The local model is allowed to learn pixel generation, but the project must
store the drawing-process data that shaped the image. A generated image without
its drawing-process package is not acceptable for training history.

## Hard failures:

| Failure | Meaning |
|---|---|
| missing_drawing_process | Generation did not store the drawing-process data. |
| skipped_spatial_blockout | Image jumped into texture/detail without a readable layout blockout. |
| skipped_value_grouping | Image has materials but no readable light/dark structure. |
| skipped_grounding_pass | Objects and edges were not integrated into terrain. |
| polish_without_structure | Image has detail but lacks professional map structure. |

# ecology-state-rules

Type: ecology
Version: v0.2
Updated: 2026-07-08 12:52:59 +08:00
Status: draft for owner review

## Purpose

This file defines natural logic for the Earth-like first playable world. Ecology
prevents the image from becoming random green noise, decoration scatter, or a
collage of unrelated vegetation.

## Required Ecology Data

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| biomeType | First version defaults to temperate natural home unless version changes. |
| moistureLevel | Influences grass color, mud, water edge, reeds, and moss density. |
| growthStage | Controls young, normal, dense, or overgrown vegetation. |
| vegetationDensity | Controls detail density without turning the frame into noise. |
| waterInfluence | Controls shoreline plants, wet ground, and blue-green reflection. |
| pathWear | Controls how grass is worn down along the route. |
| seasonState | Future state field for color and growth variation. |

## Natural Relationship Rules

| Relationship | Requirement |
|---|---|
| grass near path | Slightly worn, lower, and less dense near the path. |
| grass near water | Cooler, wetter, with reeds or shoreline plants when allowed. |
| forest edge | Denser vegetation near boundary, but not a flat vertical wall. |
| rocks | Should sit in plausible ground pockets, not float over grass. |
| flowers | Small accents, not random high-contrast noise. |
| mud | Appears near path wear, water influence, or low ground; not random smears. |

## Training Use

Ecology data must feed generation tasks as structured fields, not only text.
The local model should learn that grass, water, path, objects, and boundary are
related natural systems.

## Hard failures:

| Failure | Meaning |
|---|---|
| ecology_random_noise | Natural details look randomly sprayed rather than ecologically related. |
| vegetation_density_overload | Vegetation density hides map structure or route readability. |
| water_ecology_mismatch | Water edge lacks wetland, shore, or transition logic. |
| path_wear_missing | Path does not affect surrounding grass or ground. |
| biome_style_mismatch | Plants, terrain, and color imply conflicting biomes. |

# playability-contract

Type: gameplay
Version: v0.2
Updated: 2026-07-08 12:52:59 +08:00
Status: draft for owner review

## Purpose

This file defines what makes the map playable instead of merely decorative. The
first player-facing world map must communicate movement, blocked areas, points
of interest, and future interaction affordances.

## Player Readability Requirements

| Requirement | Meaning |
|---|---|
| start readability | Player can identify where entry begins. |
| route readability | Player can follow the main path without guessing. |
| destination readability | Player can identify the home center or main focus. |
| blocked readability | Water, dense objects, or boundaries explain where the player cannot go. |
| interaction readability | Important objects can later become clickable without visual confusion. |
| scale readability | The player can understand path width, object footprint, and usable space. |

## Gameplay Fields

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| walkableRegionIds | Regions where movement is allowed. |
| collisionRegionIds | Regions that block movement. |
| interactionPointIds | Potential click, collect, build, inspect, or care targets. |
| routeGraph | Entrance-to-center and branch route graph. |
| affordanceVisualCues | Visual hints that an object or region matters. |
| playerScaleReference | Implied scale for avatar/pet movement. |

## First Version Gameplay Scope

| Feature | Scope |
|---|---|
| movement | Must be visually supported even if full control is not finished. |
| interaction | Must reserve clear object/region cues for later interaction. |

# complete-map-grammar

Type: map-grammar
Version: v0.2
Updated: 2026-07-08 12:52:59 +08:00
Status: draft for owner review

## Purpose

This file defines how a complete first playable map is composed. A local crop,
material slot, texture tile, or object preview can train a sub-skill, but it
cannot pass as the game map. The complete RuntimeFrame must satisfy map grammar.

## Required Complete Map Parts

| Part | Requirement | Pass cue |
|---|---|---|
| entrance | One readable entry region from edge or lower-side approach. | Player understands where the map begins. |
| main path | Natural dirt path or worn route from entrance toward home center. | Route is continuous, grounded, and readable. |
| home center | Central playable clearing or focal area. | Player understands the main destination. |
| branch path | Optional secondary path to water, resource, or boundary. | Supports exploration without confusing main route. |
| water edge | Water and shore region on one side or corner. | Water reads as water and shore is not a pasted wall. |
| natural boundary | Forest edge, rocks, water, or terrain limit. | Map feels bounded without hard rectangular clipping. |
| object clusters | Trees, rocks, shrubs, flowers, reeds. | Details support structure instead of random scatter. |
| open playable space | Clear walkable grass/clearing around route and center. | Player can imagine movement. |

## Layout Ratios

| Area | First-version target |
|---|---|
| walkable/open area | Large enough to read gameplay and route; avoid total texture carpet. |
| water area | Visible but not dominant unless version scope says water map. |
| path area | Clear but not oversized pasted band. |
| dense object area | Mostly near boundary, water edge, or natural clusters. |
| central focus | Must not be swallowed by texture noise or decoration. |

## Composition Rules

| Rule | Requirement |
|---|---|
| first glance | The frame must read as a playable game map in one glance. |
| route hierarchy | Main path is more important than branch path. |
| edge integration | Shoreline, forest edge, and boundaries must transition naturally. |
| scale unity | Objects, terrain texture, and path width must share one scale language. |
| no collage | No region should look copied from a different camera, palette, or asset source. |

## Hard failures:

| Failure | Meaning |
|---|---|
| missing_complete_map_part | One or more required map parts are absent. |
| route_hierarchy_missing | Main and branch routes cannot be distinguished. |
| center_swallowed_by_texture | Home center exists but is unreadable because of texture or clutter. |
| boundary_hard_clip | Map edge reads as cropped rectangle rather than natural boundary. |
| random_asset_scatter | Objects do not support route, center, water edge, or boundary grammar. |

# professional-map-quality-rubric

Type: quality-rubric
Version: v0.2
Updated: 2026-07-08 13:37:48 +08:00
Status: draft for owner review

## Purpose

This file defines the professional quality rubric used by machine review,
agent-assisted early review, and owner final review. It turns "looks good" into
scored data for training and failure repair.

## Score Categories

| Category | Weight | Pass requirement |
|---|---:|---|
| game_read | 20 | First glance reads as playable game map. |
| map_grammar | 20 | Entrance, route, center, water edge and boundary are readable. |
| material_quality | 15 | Grass, path, water, shore and objects read correctly. |
| style_unity | 15 | Camera, palette, scale, lighting and abstraction are unified. |
| grounding | 10 | Objects and transitions sit naturally in the world. |
| gameplay_readability | 10 | Movement, collision and interaction affordances are understandable. |
| polish | 10 | No debug, placeholder, noise, collage or training-preview feeling. |

Passing a machine score does not override owner review. Owner rejection becomes
a valid negative training signal.

## Grade Bands

| Score | Meaning | Action |
|---|---|---|
| 90-100 | Professional candidate | Owner review and possible promotion. |
| 75-89 | Strong near-pass | Record failures and repair targeted issues. |
| 60-74 | Useful training candidate | Train from positives/negatives but do not promote. |
| 40-59 | Failed map candidate | Negative sample with failure codes. |
| 0-39 | Blocked | Do not use except as negative diagnostic. |

## Required Review Output

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| reviewId | Stable review record id. |
| dictionaryVersionId | Dictionary used for review. |
| runtimeFrameId | RuntimeFrame/candidate being reviewed. |
| modelCheckpointId | Model/checkpoint that generated it. |
| categoryScores | Score for each category above. |
| totalScore | Weighted total. |
| passStatus | pass, near_pass, fail, blocked, owner_pending. |
| failureCodes | Structured failure codes. |
| ownerReview | pending, accepted, rejected. |
| nextFixTargets | Specific dictionary entries and tasks to repair. |

## Hard failures:

| Failure | Meaning |
|---|---|
| quality_rubric_missing | Review did not use the professional map quality rubric. |
| quality_score_unstructured | Review result lacks category scores and structured failure codes. |
| machine_score_overrides_owner | Machine score incorrectly overrides owner rejection. |
| near_pass_without_fix_targets | Near-pass frame lacks next repair targets. |
| professional_score_below_gate | Frame score is below professional display gate. |

# runtime-render-layer-recipe

Type: render-layer-recipe
Version: v0.2
Updated: 2026-07-08 13:37:48 +08:00
Status: draft for owner review

## Purpose

This file defines the intended rendering and compositing order for a complete
RuntimeFrame. It prevents the model or compositor from creating collage,
floating objects, hidden routes, or broken layer relationships.

## Render Layer Order

| Order | Layer | Requirement |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | base terrain | Grass/open ground establishes readable land. |
| 2 | water mass | Water region placed before shoreline detail. |
| 3 | major path | Main path and branch path embedded into ground. |
| 4 | shoreline transition | Land-water edge integrates water and grass. |
| 5 | boundary mass | Forest edge, rocks or terrain boundary frames the map. |
| 6 | object footprints | Ground contact areas for trees, rocks, shrubs. |
| 7 | objects | Trees, rocks, shrubs, flowers, reeds, pebbles. |
| 8 | contact shadows | Small grounding shadows or dark bases. |
| 9 | gameplay cues | Subtle cues for route, center and interaction. |
| 10 | polish details | Final texture/detail pass with noise control. |

## Layer Binding Data

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| layerId | Stable render layer id. |
| layerType | base, terrain, transition, object, shadow, cue, polish. |
| inputSource | World fact, material recipe, object recipe or compositor rule. |
| spatialBinding | Region/layer record this render layer expresses. |
| occlusionRule | What this layer may cover or must preserve. |
| failureCodes | Failure codes when layer breaks. |

## Layer Rules

| Rule | Requirement |
|---|---|
| route_preserved | Detail and objects must not hide the main route. |
| center_preserved | Objects and texture must not bury home center. |
| contact_before_object | Object footprint/contact must exist before object reads as valid. |
| transition_before_polish | Shore/path transitions must be solved before detail polish. |
| no_debug_fallback | Program fallback or debug drawing cannot be presented as final visual layer. |

## Hard failures:

| Failure | Meaning |
|---|---|
| render_layer_recipe_missing | Generation or compositor lacks render layer recipe. |
| render_layer_order_broken | Layers are composed in an order that breaks readability. |
| route_occluded_by_detail | Main route is hidden by details or objects. |
| center_occluded_by_detail | Home center is hidden by texture or objects. |
| object_without_contact_layer | Object appears without footprint/contact layer. |
| debug_layer_visible | Debug/fallback/program layer is visible as final game art. |

# single-map-visual-acceptance

Type: review dictionary
Version: v0.2
Updated: 2026-07-08 14:03:25 +08:00
Status: active draft scope for owner review

## Purpose

This file defines the current acceptance standard for the single complete map
visual. It deliberately excludes player character, interaction mechanics,
collection/building gameplay, and multi-tick dynamic variation.

## Active Acceptance Gates

| Gate | Requirement |
|---|---|
| single_map_scope | Frame is one complete map visual, not local crop or gameplay demo. |
| map_structure | Entrance, main route, center, water edge and natural boundary are readable. |
| material_quality | Grass, path, water, shoreline, boundary and objects read professionally. |
| composition_quality | Read order, focal hierarchy, open space and balance are clear. |
| art_direction | Camera, palette, scale, light and abstraction are unified. |
| object_grounding | Trees, rocks, shrubs and details sit naturally in terrain. |
| storage_trace | Image, task package, model id, review and failure codes are stored. |
| owner_review | Owner may reject even if machine gates pass. |

## Reserved Non-Gates

| Reserved area | Current rule |
|---|---|
| player character | Must not be required. |
| player movement mechanics | Must not decide pass/fail. |
| click/collect/build/inspect interaction | Must not decide pass/fail. |
| multi-tick state change | Must not decide pass/fail. |
| UI markers | Must not be required for map readability. |

## Current Pass Definition

```txt
Pass = one complete professional natural-home map visual
+ map structure readable
+ material and ecology coherent
+ composition professionally organized
+ objects grounded
+ no player/interaction dependency
+ full automatic storage and review trace
+ owner accepts
```

| Failure | Meaning |
|---|---|
| single_map_acceptance_missing | Review did not use the current single-map acceptance standard. |

# live-map-state

Type: runtime-state
Version: v0.2
Updated: 2026-07-08 12:52:59 +08:00
Status: draft for owner review

## Purpose

This file defines how the visual dictionary connects to a live world. A
RuntimeFrame is a snapshot of a world tick. It must be possible to regenerate,
review, and compare later frames when the world changes.

## Required Runtime Fields

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| worldId | Stable world identifier. |
| ownerId | Owner/player identifier. |
| tick | Current world tick. |
| dictionaryVersionId | Visual dictionary version used to interpret the frame. |
| runtimeFrameId | Stored RuntimeFrame record id. |
| sourceFactIds | World facts used to generate the frame. |
| stateDiffIds | Changes since the previous visual frame. |
| visualGenerationTaskId | Structured generation task used by the local model. |
| reviewRecordId | Review record produced after generation. |

## Live Change Types

| Change type | Visual impact |
|---|---|
| growth | Vegetation density, color, or object maturity may change. |
| construction | Center, route, or object focus may change if facts allow it. |
| resource | Wood, stone, plant materials, or water access may become visible or depleted. |
| weather | Future visual modifier; first version may reserve fields only. |
| season | Future color/growth modifier; first version may reserve fields only. |
| damage_repair | Future state modifier for objects or paths. |

## Runtime Rules

| Rule | Requirement |
|---|---|
| stable identity | The same world should feel continuous across ticks. |
| controlled variation | Changes must be caused by state diffs, not random model drift. |
| no fact rewrite | Visual repair cannot rewrite world facts. |
| replayable review | Stored generation task and review record must reproduce why a frame passed or failed. |

## Hard failures:

| Failure | Meaning |
|---|---|
| tick_unbound_frame | Frame is not bound to worldId and tick. |
| state_diff_untraceable | Visual change cannot be traced to runtime state. |
| unstable_world_identity | Same world changes style or layout without a state reason. |
| visual_repair_rewrites_facts | Visual fix changes stored world facts instead of regenerating expression. |
| missing_review_link | RuntimeFrame lacks link to generation and review records. |

# runtime-frame-state-binding-schema

Type: runtime-state
Version: v0.2
Updated: 2026-07-08 13:53:29 +08:00
Status: draft for owner review

## Purpose

This file defines the executable binding between live world state, generation
task, RuntimeFrame, generated image, review record, and next fix target. A game
map is alive because every frame belongs to a world, tick, and state history.

## Runtime Frame State Binding Schema

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---:|---|
| bindingId | string | Yes | Stable id for this binding record. |
| schemaVersion | string | Yes | Must be `runtime-frame-state-binding-v1`. |
| createdAt | datetime | Yes | Detailed timestamp. |
| dictionaryVersionId | string | Yes | Dictionary version used for generation/review. |
| worldId | string | Yes | Runtime world id. |
| ownerId | string | Yes | Owner/player id. |
| tick | number | Yes | Runtime tick represented by the frame. |
| previousTick | number nullable | Yes | Previous tick if available. |
| runtimeFrameId | string | Yes | RuntimeFrame record id. |
| visualGenerationTaskId | string | Yes | Generation task package id. |
| directorRunId | string | Yes | Director output id that created the task. |
| generatedAssetId | string | Yes | Generated image/asset id and hash record. |
| reviewRecordId | string | Yes | Machine/dictionary/owner review record id. |
| sourceFactIds | string[] | Yes | World facts represented by the frame. |
| stateDiffIds | string[] | Yes | State changes from previous tick/frame. |
| entityRecordIds | string[] | Yes | World entity records visible or relevant in this frame. |
| spatialLayerRecordIds | string[] | Yes | Spatial-grid layer records bound to the frame. |
| failureCodes | string[] | Yes | Current review failures, if any. |
| nextFixTargetIds | string[] | Yes | Dictionary entries or task fields to repair next. |
| canEnterWorld | boolean | Yes | Whether gates allow the frame into `/world`. |

## State Diff Types

| stateDiffType | Meaning |
|---|---|
| no_change | Frame is a stable re-render of same state. |
| growth_change | Vegetation or natural growth changed. |
| resource_change | Visible resources changed. |
| construction_change | Build/focus state changed. |
| path_wear_change | Route wear or accessibility changed. |
| water_edge_change | Moisture, waterline or shore state changed. |
| review_repair_change | Visual changed due to previous review repair. |

## Binding Rules

| Rule | Requirement |
|---|---|
| one_frame_one_binding | Every candidate RuntimeFrame must have one binding record. |
| generation_trace_required | Binding must include directorRunId and visualGenerationTaskId. |
| asset_trace_required | Binding must include generatedAssetId and image hash through asset record. |
| review_trace_required | Binding must include reviewRecordId before latest pointer can advance. |
| state_trace_required | Binding must include sourceFactIds and stateDiffIds. |
| world_gate_required | canEnterWorld may be true only after runtime, dictionary and owner gates pass. |

## Hard failures:

| Failure | Meaning |
|---|---|
| runtime_binding_schema_missing_field | Runtime frame state binding lacks required fields. |
| runtime_binding_missing_generation_trace | Binding lacks director or generation task id. |
| runtime_binding_missing_asset_trace | Binding lacks generated asset id or image hash link. |
| runtime_binding_missing_review_trace | Binding lacks review record id. |
| runtime_binding_missing_state_trace | Binding lacks sourceFactIds or stateDiffIds. |
| runtime_binding_world_gate_bypass | canEnterWorld is true without required review gates. |

# grid-and-layer-contract

Type: spatial-grid
Version: v0.2
Updated: 2026-07-08 12:52:59 +08:00
Status: draft for owner review

## Purpose

This file defines the spatial contract behind the image. A professional game map
is not only pixels. It must connect visual regions to coordinates, layers,
walkable areas, collision areas, interaction points, and live state.

## Coordinate Model

| Concept | First-version rule |
|---|---|
| frame size | Complete RuntimeFrame target is 1024x768 unless version scope changes. |
| origin | Top-left image coordinate for visual output; world-space adapter may map it to grid coordinates. |
| grid unit | Runtime may use tile/chunk abstraction; visual output must preserve readable regions. |
| active area | Main playable area must be visually clear and not hidden by decoration. |
| safe margin | Critical gameplay markers should not be placed at cropped or blocked edges. |

## Required Layers

| Layer | Meaning | Visual requirement |
|---|---|---|
| terrain layer | Base grass, water, mud, shore, path | Must be readable under all objects. |
| structure layer | Entrance, route, center, boundary | Must be readable at first glance. |
| object layer | Trees, rocks, shrubs, flowers, reeds | Must be grounded and scale-consistent. |
| walkable layer | Where the player can move | Must align with road, grass clearing, and open zones. |
| collision layer | Where the player is blocked | Must align with water, dense trees, rocks, cliffs, or boundaries. |
| interaction layer | Clickable or usable points | Must be visually discoverable without clutter. |
| state layer | Tick-dependent changes | Must not break previous layers. |

## Spatial Rules

| Rule | Requirement |
|---|---|
| visual-to-logic match | The player should not see a walkable-looking region that is actually blocked without reason. |
| collision readability | Water, dense forest, rock mass, and boundary must visually explain blocked movement. |
| route continuity | Main path must connect entrance, center, and optional branch zones without visual interruption. |
| object footprint | Objects must reserve ground contact and cannot float over walkable routes. |
| layer audit | RuntimeFrame record must be able to count terrain, object, walkable, collision, interaction, and state layers. |

## Database Planning

Future database tables must store spatial layer records separately from the
rendered image so the same world can be reviewed, replayed, and re-rendered.

| Table concept | Required links |
|---|---|
| spatial_grid_version | dictionaryVersionId, worldId, frameVersion |
| spatial_region | regionId, layerType, polygon/tile range, sourceFactId |
| layer_binding | visualRegionId, spatialRegionId, reviewStatus |
| interaction_binding | interactionId, spatialRegionId, visualCueId |

## Hard failures:

| Failure | Meaning |
|---|---|
| visual_logic_mismatch | Visual walkability or collision does not match runtime layer meaning. |
| unreadable_walkable_area | Player cannot tell where movement is allowed. |
| unreadable_collision_area | Blocked regions are not visually justified. |
| broken_route_continuity | The path is visually interrupted or disconnected. |
| object_footprint_missing | Objects lack clear contact footprint in spatial layer. |

The model must learn grass as structured living terrain, not as a noisy green fill.

| Field | Requirement |
|---|---|

| local_detail | Flowers, leaves and small stems are accents, not the primary grass identity. |
| contamination_guard | Water, road, shoreline and object fragments must not appear inside the grass material slot. |
| repeat_guard | Grass must avoid obvious repeated tile grids and mechanical stamps. |

# grass

Type: terrain
World meaning: ordinary walkable natural grassland
Version: v0.1

Grass is the primary ground of the first natural home. It must make the map
feel alive and readable without becoming visual noise.

| Field | Definition |
|---|---|
| color | Layered natural greens with small warm/cool variation. Avoid single flat green and toxic neon green. |
| texture | Short grass, moss, tiny soil specks and soft leaf clusters. Texture should be visible but not dirty. |
| density | Medium. More detail near edges and objects, calmer in readable walkable open areas. |
| walkability | Usually walkable unless overlaid by object/collision facts. |
| transitions | Blends into dirt path, tall grass, mud and shoreline through irregular feathered edges. |
| light | Receives shared daylight and subtle shadows from objects. |

Positive signs:

| Sign | Meaning |
|---|---|
| layered_green | Multiple natural green values, not a flat fill. |
| clean_readable_surface | Player can still read the ground as playable. |
| local_detail | Small grass/leaf details enrich without hiding structure. |

| Failure | Meaning |
|---|---|
| green_noise_field | Grass reads as random noise or dirty texture. |

# automatic-storage

Type: training rule
Version: v0.1

The local program, not Codex memory, must store every important training and
inference artifact. Codex may help during early owner review, but the target is
that the small model and project pipeline keep complete evidence themselves.

## Dead Rule

All training content must come from stored records.

| Rule | Requirement |
|---|---|
| no_unstored_training_content | A generated image, training sample, review, failure, success or candidate cannot be shown as training content unless it has a stored record. |
| no_conversation_memory_source | Conversation text is not a training source. It can only explain or create a stored record. |
| no_direct_preview_only | A page preview is not enough. The image path, input path, model/checkpoint id, review result and labels must be stored. |
| page_reads_storage | UI pages must read training content from stored files or future database records, not from temporary in-memory state. |
| every_trial_has_record | Every dictionary trial must include a review record and a stored image. |

## Required Automatic Storage

| Artifact | Required |
|---|---|
| generated image | Yes, every inference. |
| structured input | Yes, prompt/schema/world facts used to generate. |
| model checkpoint id | Yes, if model generated the result. |
| runtime frame json | Yes, when a full map frame exists. |
| machine review result | Yes. |
| owner review result | Yes when owner gives judgment. |
| failure codes | Yes for every failed or weak sample. |
| next training target | Yes, even if only one target is known. |

## Division of Responsibility

| Actor | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| local program | Store images, metadata, model ids, review results and latest pointers. |
| small model | Produce inference output and later consume accepted/rejected evidence. |
| Codex | Help build pipeline, diagnose failure and translate owner review into data. |
| owner | Give final early-stage visual acceptance or rejection. |

Hard failures:

| Failure | Meaning |
|---|---|
| inference_not_saved | Model output was generated but not stored. |
| review_not_saved | Review happened but cannot be found in project records. |
| no_negative_memory | Failed outputs are not available for future training. |
| unstored_training_content | Training content is visible or discussed but has no stored record. |
| page_bypasses_storage | Page shows training content without reading the stored record first. |

# feedback-loop

Type: training dictionary
Version: v0.1

The model must learn from both technical failures and owner visual failures.

```txt
RuntimeFrame generated
-> machine review
-> owner review if machine passes
-> label as positive or negative
-> attach failure codes
-> select dictionary fix targets
-> build next training plan
-> rerun model
```

Rules:

| Rule | Definition |
|---|---|
| no_unlabeled_training | A generated frame cannot train future model without positive/negative decision. |
| owner_failure_is_data | Owner rejection is not subjective noise; it is a high-value negative sample. |
| dictionary_code_required | Every rejection must map to one or more dictionary failure codes. |
| no_metric_chasing_only | Do not train only to pass numerical gates if owner visual quality fails. |
| preserve_failed_images | Failed images must remain archived for audit and training. |

# current-single-map-visual-scope

Type: version boundary
Version: v0.2
Updated: 2026-07-08 13:58:07 +08:00
Status: active draft scope for owner review

## Purpose

This file defines the current active work scope. The project architecture keeps
gameplay, player, collision, interaction and live-world concepts, but the active
training and review target is now only one complete professional map image.

## Active Scope

| Area | Current status | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| complete map visual | Active | The generated frame must be one complete natural-home map. |
| map grammar | Active | Entrance, main route, center, water edge and natural boundary must read clearly. |
| terrain material | Active | Grass, path, water, shoreline, mud and forest edge must look professional. |
| object grounding | Active | Trees, rocks, shrubs, flowers, reeds and details must sit in the map. |
| art direction | Active | The frame must look like one unified player-facing game map. |
| quality review | Active | Review uses map visual quality, material, composition and art direction. |

## Reserved Architecture

| Area | Current status | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| player character | Reserved | Do not draw or train player character now. |
| player movement | Reserved | Do not judge movement mechanics now. |
| interaction/click targets | Reserved | Do not train click, collect, build or inspect behavior now. |
| gameplay loop | Reserved | Do not require gameplay systems for current map visual pass. |
| dynamic tick variation | Reserved | Keep runtime fields, but do not require multi-frame state variation now. |
| collision implementation | Reserved | Keep spatial concept, but do not block the current visual map pass on gameplay collision. |

## Current Generation Rule

The local model should generate a complete single-map visual candidate:

```txt
single complete natural-home map
+ no player character
+ no clickable interaction target requirement
+ no collect/build/inspect gameplay requirement
+ no dynamic multi-tick visual requirement
+ focus on professional terrain, structure, composition, material and art direction
```

## Current Review Rule

| Review area | Active now |
|---|---:|
| complete-map composition | Yes |
| material quality | Yes |
| art direction | Yes |
| object grounding | Yes |
| route/center/water/boundary readability | Yes |
| player movement mechanics | No |
| interaction affordance mechanics | No |
| construction/collection mechanics | No |
| multi-tick state change | No |

## Hard failures:

| Failure | Meaning |

training preview or placeholder.

material crop and not a gameplay interaction demo.

# entity-taxonomy

Type: world-ontology
Version: v0.2
Updated: 2026-07-08 12:52:59 +08:00
Status: draft for owner review

## Purpose

This file defines what can exist in the first playable AI-PET-WORLD map before
visual generation happens. AI Painter must not decide world facts by itself. It
may express stored facts, but it cannot invent major terrain, buildings,
characters, resources, road systems, or story outcomes.

## Required Entity Groups

| Entity group | First-version scope | Visual dependency |
|---|---|---|
| world | world id, owner id, tick, seed, version | Required by every RuntimeFrame. |
| terrain | grass, water, shoreline, dirt path, mud patch, forest edge | Required by map grammar and visual layers. |
| structure | entrance, main path, branch path, home center, boundary | Required for game readability. |
| object | tree, rock, shrub, flower, grass detail, pebble, reed | Required for natural detail and grounding. |
| resource | wood, stone, plant material, water access | May appear only when world facts allow it. |
| construction | planned or active home/construction focus | May appear only when runtime construction state allows it. |
| interaction | clickable/collectible/buildable point | Must map to gameplay and spatial layers. |
| state | growth, damage, readiness, wetness, season, time | Drives live map variation. |

## Required Fields

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| entityId | Stable id used by runtime, visual generation, review, and database records. |
| entityType | One of the entity groups above. |
| displayName | Human-readable owner-facing name. |
| worldMeaning | What the entity means in the game world. |
| allowedVisualForms | Which visual dictionary entries may express the entity. |
| placementDomain | Which spatial regions may contain the entity. |
| lifecycleState | Current live state, such as planned, active, grown, blocked, damaged. |
| sourceFactId | Runtime fact id that proves this entity exists. |

## Director Rules

| Rule | Requirement |
|---|---|
| fact first | Director reads entities from runtime facts before creating visual tasks. |
| no invention | Director may not add major entities to improve composition. |
| visual substitution | If the local model cannot render an entity, the frame must fail instead of substituting unrelated art. |
| source binding | Every visible major entity must be traceable to sourceFactId or dictionary version scope. |

## Hard failures:

| Failure | Meaning |
|---|---|
| invented_major_entity | The image contains major buildings, roads, characters, objects, or events not present in world facts. |
| missing_required_entity | A required first-version structure or terrain entity is absent. |
| unbound_visible_entity | A visible major entity cannot be traced to world facts or version scope. |
| entity_scope_mismatch | The image shows a feature outside the current dictionary version boundary. |

# world-entity-record-schema

Type: world-ontology
Version: v0.2
Updated: 2026-07-08 13:53:29 +08:00
Status: draft for owner review

## Purpose

This file defines the executable schema for world entities that may be expressed
in visual generation. The local model must not invent entity existence. It may
only express entities from version scope or runtime source facts.

## World Entity Record Schema

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---:|---|
| entityRecordId | string | Yes | Stable id for this entity record. |
| dictionaryVersionId | string | Yes | Dictionary version that defines the entity rules. |
| worldId | string | Yes | Runtime world id when entity is runtime-bound. |
| tick | number nullable | Yes | Runtime tick when entity state is tick-bound. |
| entityType | string | Yes | world, terrain, structure, object, resource, construction, interaction, state. |
| entityName | string | Yes | Direct kebab-case name, such as `main-path`, `tree`, `water-edge`. |
| displayName | string | Yes | Owner/player readable name. |
| worldMeaning | string | Yes | What this entity means inside the game world. |
| visualMeaning | string | Yes | What the player should understand visually. |
| sourceKind | string | Yes | version_scope, runtime_fact, generated_state, owner_defined. |
| sourceFactId | string nullable | Yes | Runtime fact id when required. |
| allowedVisualEntryIds | string[] | Yes | Dictionary entries that may visually express this entity. |
| placementDomainIds | string[] | Yes | Map parts or spatial domains where entity may appear. |
| lifecycleState | string | Yes | planned, active, grown, blocked, depleted, damaged, repaired, reserved. |
| visibilityRule | string | Yes | required, allowed, conditional, hidden, forbidden. |
| gameplayRole | string | Yes | none, movement, collision, interaction, resource, construction, focus. |
| reviewFailureCodes | string[] | Yes | Failure codes if entity is missing, invented or visually wrong. |

## Entity Type Rules

| entityType | Required source | First-version examples |
|---|---|---|
| world | runtime_fact | world id, owner id, tick, seed, version |
| terrain | version_scope or runtime_fact | grass, water, shoreline, dirt path |
| structure | version_scope or runtime_fact | entrance, main path, home center, boundary |
| object | version_scope or runtime_fact | tree, rock, shrub, flower, reed |
| resource | runtime_fact | wood, stone, water access, plant material |
| construction | runtime_fact | planned home center, active build focus |
| interaction | runtime_fact or reserved | clickable, collectable, buildable, inspectable |
| state | runtime_fact or generated_state | growth, wetness, season, readiness |

## Visibility Rules

| visibilityRule | Meaning |
|---|---|
| required | Must appear in first-version complete RuntimeFrame. |
| allowed | May appear if it supports map grammar. |
| conditional | May appear only when source facts or state allow it. |
| hidden | Exists in world state but should not appear in this visual frame. |
| forbidden | Must not appear in this version/task. |

## Validation Rules

| Rule | Requirement |
|---|---|
| source_binding_required | Runtime-only entities must include sourceFactId. |
| visual_entry_required | Visible entities must point to allowedVisualEntryIds. |
| placement_required | Visible entities must include placementDomainIds. |
| gameplay_role_required | Interaction, resource and construction entities must declare gameplayRole. |
| forbidden_entity_block | Forbidden entities must not appear in generation tasks. |

## Hard failures:

| Failure | Meaning |
|---|---|
| entity_record_schema_missing_field | World entity record lacks required schema fields. |
| runtime_entity_missing_source_fact | Runtime-only entity has no sourceFactId. |
| visible_entity_missing_visual_entry | Visible entity has no allowed visual dictionary entry. |
| visible_entity_missing_placement_domain | Visible entity has no placement domain. |
| forbidden_entity_in_task | Forbidden entity appears in generation task or candidate frame. |
